title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole-Source BOA - Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC
description: 1.0 Description of Intent Army Contracting Command � Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA), intends to establish a sole-source, open-market Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Reasonable Source�), with Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC (Maple Grove, MN). The proposed BOA will establish a 5-year framework (with a 6-month FAR 52.217-8) extension option) of pre-negotiated terms and pricing to support proprietary Zeiss metrology assets, with a total estimated capacity of $9,000,000.00. The primary NAICS code for this requirement is 811219 (Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance). 2.0 Scope of Services This agreement will provide critical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and associated proprietary metrology system (e.g., Surfcom) support. The scope covers baseline requirements for Tooele Army Depot (TEAD), McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (McAAP), and Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA), and is structured to allow any other Joint Munitions Command (JMC) or Army Materiel Command (AMC) installation to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Requirements issued under this BOA will include: Software Maintenance Agreements (SMAs): Proprietary CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP software version upgrades, bug fixes, CAD driver updates, and cyber security patches Preventative Maintenance and Calibration: Annual OEM-certified physical calibrations, to include writing back to the proprietary Zeiss Computer Aided Accuracy (CAA) volumetric error compensation matrix. Emergency Repair and OEM Parts: Factory-certified repair technicians and brand-new OEM replacement parts. Zeiss Care Plus: Optional, comprehensive extended hardware warranty packages. 3.0 Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CMMs and Surfcom metrology systems and is the sole proprietary owner of the associated CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP metrology software. Zeiss does not license its software source code, nor does it share it�s proprietary diagnostic algorithms and CAA calibration matrices with third-party vendors. Consequently, only Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC or its factory-authorized technicians possess the proprietary data, diagnostic tools, and software keys required to perform these services without corrupting the equipment accuracy map or voiding current system warranties. 4.0 Response Instructions This is a Notice of Intent and is NOT a Request for Proposals (RFP) or a Request For Quote (RFQ); no solicitation is currently available. In accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Any interested vendor who believes they possess the capability and legal proprietary authorization to provide all described services (specifically including proprietary CALYPSO software updates and CAA error-matrix calibration) must submit their response via email to the Contracting Specialist, Dustin Sexton at dustin.p.sexton.civ@army.mil. Responses are due no later than 1:00pm CST on 23 September 2026 Capability statements are limited to 5 pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Replace Perimeter Fence Pasture 7
description: Amendment 00001 Posted 9/10/2026 - Amendment incoporates questions and answers as well as four new Solicitation Attachments. Solicitation Due date has not changed and is still scheduled to close on September 23rd, 2026 1300 Central Daylight Time. IAW Attachment 1 - Statement of Work, The Livestock Arthropod Pest Research Unit (LAPRU) includes the Cattle Fever Tick Research Laboratory (CFTRL), which operates under biosecurity at the USDA Moore Air Base near Edinburg, Texas. This is a satellite facility of the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory (KBUSLIRL) in Kerrville, Texas. Scientific endeavors at the CFTRL deliver technologies that the USDA Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program can integrate to keep the U.S. free of cattle fever ticks in a sustainable manner. This ensures continued prosperity of the U.S. livestock industry. Unique assets at the CFTRL include cattle fever tick colonies, barns for studies with cattle that can be artificially infested with ticks, and pastures providing the ability to conduct studies with infested cattle resembling field conditions. However, modernization of the facilities is required to keep up with the expansion of the research program at the CFTRL that is underway to meet the expectations of the U.S. livestock industry and other stakeholders� groups. The current perimeter fence around pasture 7 is allowing wildlife onto the facility. This puts the facility at risk of losing our quarantine zones.

title: Sole Source to Diaconia LLC for Audio-Visual Renovation--Bluemont, VA
description: The intent of this information technology and audio visual (IT/AV) refresh is to upgrade current systems and components with new/upgraded system/components in three distinct spaces in addition to any necessary cabling and connections between these spaces and within the FEMA Operations Center (FOC) and Continuity of Operations (COOP) facility. This contract will be sole sourced to Diaconia LLC. Diaconia and Bridges SI (prime and subcontractor team) are uniquely positioned to perform this refresh because they originally engineered, installed, documented, and has continuously sustained the affected systems since 2010. The government already owns the required deliverables, including source code and record drawings, but Diaconia and Bridges SI�s value lies in its live operational knowledge, cleared and badged workforce, proprietary system expertise, and proven ability to maintain the security posture of the accredited environment. The Diaconia and Bridges SI team provide a single accountable partner for design, installation, sustainment, firmware remediation, supply chain risk management, and accreditation support. A transition to another contractor would require significant discovery, documentation recreation, code replacement, revalidation, personnel processing, and added downtime. It would also create accountability gaps between installation and sustainment, complicating warranties, troubleshooting, and mission support. Due to the secure spaces in which the renovation will be performed, contractors would have to visit the site to accurately propose to the installation scope. This could cause undue security risks. Limiting this requirement to a team that is familiar with the secure spaces, ensures the requirement will be proposed accurately and security concerns are mitigated. This requirement is for a secure, mission-critical renovation in sensitive operational spaces where contractor familiarity, cleared access, and system knowledge materially affect cost, schedule, security, and mission readiness. Additionally, all Contractor personnel must possess a valid TS/SCI Clearance, and installer�s warranty shall include 1 year of support with a requirement to provide on-site support within 12 hours for all warrantied equipment.

title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole-Source BOA - Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC
description: 1.0 Description of Intent Army Contracting Command � Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA), intends to establish a sole-source, open-market Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Reasonable Source�), with Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC (Maple Grove, MN). The proposed BOA will establish a 5-year framework (with a 6-month FAR 52.217-8) extension option) of pre-negotiated terms and pricing to support proprietary Zeiss metrology assets, with a total estimated capacity of $9,000,000.00. The primary NAICS code for this requirement is 811219 (Other Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance). 2.0 Scope of Services This agreement will provide critical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) and associated proprietary metrology system (e.g., Surfcom) support. The scope covers baseline requirements for Tooele Army Depot (TEAD), McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (McAAP), and Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA), and is structured to allow any other Joint Munitions Command (JMC), Army Materiel Command (AMC), Army Sustainment Command (ASC), and Tank-Automotive & Armaments Command (TACOM) CONUS installations to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Installations including but not limited to: -Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) - Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) - Letterkenny Munitions Center (LEMC) - Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC) to bilaterally on-ramp their proprietary Zeiss assets. Requirements issued under this BOA will include: Software Maintenance Agreements (SMAs): Proprietary CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP software version upgrades, bug fixes, CAD driver updates, and cyber security patches Preventative Maintenance and Calibration: Annual OEM-certified physical calibrations, to include writing back to the proprietary Zeiss Computer Aided Accuracy (CAA) volumetric error compensation matrix. Emergency Repair and OEM Parts: Factory-certified repair technicians and brand-new OEM replacement parts. Zeiss Care Plus: Optional, comprehensive extended hardware warranty packages. 3.0 Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the CMMs and Surfcom metrology systems and is the sole proprietary owner of the associated CALYPSO and Surfcom MAP metrology software. Zeiss does not license its software source code, nor does it share it�s proprietary diagnostic algorithms and CAA calibration matrices with third-party vendors. Consequently, only Carl Zeiss Industrial Quality Solutions, LLC or its factory-authorized technicians possess the proprietary data, diagnostic tools, and software keys required to perform these services without corrupting the equipment accuracy map or voiding current system warranties. 4.0 Response Instructions This is a Notice of Intent and is NOT a Request for Proposals (RFP) or a Request For Quote (RFQ); no solicitation is currently available. In accordance with FAR 5.207(c)(16)(ii), all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Any interested vendor who believes they possess the capability and legal proprietary authorization to provide all described services (specifically including proprietary CALYPSO software updates and CAA error-matrix calibration) must submit their response via email to the Contracting Specialist, Dustin Sexton at dustin.p.sexton.civ@army.mil. Responses are due no later than 1:00pm CST on 23 September 2026 Capability statements are limited to 5 pages. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.

description: IAW Attachment 1 - Statement of Work, The Livestock Arthropod Pest Research Unit (LAPRU) includes the Cattle Fever Tick Research Laboratory (CFTRL), which operates under biosecurity at the USDA Moore Air Base near Edinburg, Texas. This is a satellite facility of the Knipling-Bushland U.S. Livestock Insects Research Laboratory (KBUSLIRL) in Kerrville, Texas. Scientific endeavors at the CFTRL deliver technologies that the USDA Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program can integrate to keep the U.S. free of cattle fever ticks in a sustainable manner. This ensures continued prosperity of the U.S. livestock industry. Unique assets at the CFTRL include cattle fever tick colonies, barns for studies with cattle that can be artificially infested with ticks, and pastures providing the ability to conduct studies with infested cattle resembling field conditions. However, modernization of the facilities is required to keep up with the expansion of the research program at the CFTRL that is underway to meet the expectations of the U.S. livestock industry and other stakeholders� groups. The current perimeter fence around pasture 7 is allowing wildlife onto the facility. This puts the facility at risk of losing our quarantine zones.

title: Medical Device Development Instructor- Led Training
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Proposed Period of Performance: November 2�3, 2026 (Two-Day Training) Place of Performance: Constitution Center, Washington, DC Product Service Code (PSC): U004 � Education/Training � Scientific/Management NAICS Code: 611430 � Professional and Management Development Training Size Standard: $15 million NOTE: All prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) to be eligible for contract award. 1. Purpose The Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) is conducting market research to identify potential contractors capable of providing an in-person, instructor-led course on Device Development for Scientists. The course will focus on the regulatory, scientific, and commercial considerations involved in developing medical devices, obtaining U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance or approval, and successfully bringing medical devices to market. The Contractor shall provide qualified instructor(s) and all required course materials. The proposed training will be conducted over two days, November 2�3, 2026, at the Constitution Center in Washington, DC. Alternative dates may be considered based on instructor availability and mutual agreement. A copy of the Statement of Objectives (SOO) is attached to this Sources Sought Notice/RFI. 2. Scope The Contractor shall provide in-person, instructor-led training on Device Development for Scientists for up to 30 participants at the Constitution Center in Washington, DC. The Contractor shall be responsible for developing and providing all course materials, including presentation slides, workbooks, handouts, and other instructional materials. All electronic course materials shall comply with applicable Section 508 accessibility requirements. Final course materials shall be submitted to the Contracting Officer (CO) at least two business days prior to the start of the training. 3. Learning Objectives The training should address, at a minimum, the following topics: Discovery Pathways Diagnostics Therapeutics Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Target identification and validation Device Discovery and Concept Development Preclinical development Decision milestones and go/no-go criteria Target product profile Nonclinical studies Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) and Clinical Studies IDE studies and exemptions Stages/phases of clinical studies Types of data generated during clinical studies and how the data inform subsequent study design Labeling Drafting medical device labels and package inserts Academia and Industry Key differences between medical device development in academia and industry Intellectual Property U.S. patents and exclusivity considerations Regulatory Pathways Understanding the FDA regulatory pathway Device risk classifications: Class I � Low Risk Class II � Moderate Risk Class III � High Risk De Novo Classification Regulatory submissions: 510(k) De Novo Premarket Approval (PMA) Expedited/accelerated programs: Breakthrough Devices Program Safer Technologies Program (STeP) Post-Market Considerations Medical device recalls and the post-market process Coverage, Coding, and Reimbursement FDA and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) coordination Relevant pilot programs, including RAPID and TEMPO, as applicable Coding and reimbursement considerations 4. Instructor Qualifications Proposed instructor(s) shall have: A minimum of five years of relevant experience in medical device development; Demonstrated experience with the regulatory, scientific, and commercial topics identified in this notice; Relevant educational and professional experience; and A master's degree or higher in a field related to the course subject matter. Respondents should provide resumes or curricula vitae (CVs) for proposed instructor(s) demonstrating the required qualifications and experience. 5. RFI Questions Interested parties are requested to address the following questions in their response: Are you capable of providing in-person, instructor-led classroom training covering the topics and requirements described above? Do you have relevant past performance providing similar medical device development or regulatory training? If so, please provide a brief description of your relevant experience. Are you available to provide a two-day, onsite training in Washington, DC, on November 2�3, 2026? If not, please identify alternative dates during which you would be available. Please provide an estimated cost for providing the two-day training for up to 30 attendees. The estimate should include course materials, instructor travel, and any other applicable costs. This information is requested for market research and acquisition planning purposes only. Do you currently offer this training, or similar training, through an existing Government contract vehicle, including a GSA Multiple Award Schedule? If so, please identify the applicable contract vehicle and contract number. Please provide resumes or CVs for the proposed instructor(s) demonstrating their relevant education, qualifications, and medical device development experience. 6. Response Instructions Please submit responses no later than September 23, 2026, at 2:00 PM ET to: Contracting Officer: La Vivian Peasant; Email; lavivian.peasant@hhs.gov Responses should clearly identify the company name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, UEI, business size/status, and applicable Government contract vehicles, if any. 7. Disclaimer This Sources Sought Notice/RFI is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or make an award. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this notice. The information received may be used by the Government to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including the availability and capability of potential sources.

description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes located in Bakersfield, CA and the surrounding areas within Kern County, CA. title: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) - OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) - B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement or contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) or Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Procurement Process: Early involvement, separate contracts, guaranteed maximum price and collaborative delivery. PROJECT OVERVIEW & SCOPE. Title: B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar Location: Dyess Air Force Base, Texas Scope: Construct a new 95,529 sq. ft. Low Observable Corrosion Control Hangar (LO) and a Radio Frequency Facility (RF) for the new B-21 weapons system. The project demands a highly collaborative and iterative design process to manage complexity and a critical schedule. Target Price Range (TPR): The Government has established The Government's Target Price Estimate for construction is between $280,000,000 and $300,000,000. Projected Award Date: The Government targets the formal award of the Agreement Phase 1 (Design and Preconstruction Services) on or about July 2027. Current Design is at 100%. The Government is willing to revert to a 35% design, allowing the awardee and designer the ability to collaborate during an OTA procurement process. Period of Performance (POP): The projected construction timeline is approximately 1217 calendar days following the execution of the Phase 2 Construction modification. Product Service Code (PSC): Y1BG (Construction of Electronic and Communications Facilities). NAICS Code: 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES & FEEDBACK AREAS. In accordance with Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Design Instruction #3, the Government is seeking commercial industry feedback regarding the feasibility and market capacity for the following innovative methods: Modular and Off-Site Prefabrication: Fabricating large sections of the facility or complex mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in factory-controlled environments to compress the construction schedule. 3D Printing: Utilizing large-scale 3D printing for secondary building components, non-load-bearing walls, or perimeter security fencing. Advanced Materials: Incorporating self-healing concrete to reduce lifecycle maintenance and maximize structural integrity, or utilizing high-performance insulation (e.g., aerogels or vacuum-insulated panels) to meet high-performance building standards. Submissions: Submit your capabilities statement and Market Intelligence response (attachment) via email toThomas Howard at Thomas.W.Howard@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Johnston at Nicholas.I.Johnston@usace.army.mil no later than Wednesday, September 23st, 2026 at 2:00 PM CDT (21:00 UTC). Use email subject: "Sources Sought Response: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hangar (LO/RF) Market Intel - [Your Firm Name]". File Naming Convention: Market Intel_B21 LO/RF_[FIRM NAME]

title: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hanger (LO/RF) - OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) - B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement or contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) or Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Procurement Process: Early involvement, separate contracts, guaranteed maximum price and collaborative delivery. PROJECT OVERVIEW & SCOPE. Title: B-21 Low Observable / Radio Frequency Hangar Location: Dyess Air Force Base, Texas Scope: Construct a new 95,529 sq. ft. Low Observable Corrosion Control Hangar (LO) and a Radio Frequency Facility (RF) for the new B-21 weapons system. The project demands a highly collaborative and iterative design process to manage complexity and a critical schedule. Target Price Range (TPR): The Government has established The Government's Target Price Estimate for construction is between $280,000,000 and $300,000,000. Projected Award Date: The Government targets the formal award of the Agreement Phase 1 (Design and Preconstruction Services) on or about July 2027. Current Design is at 100%. The Government is willing to revert to a 35% design, allowing the awardee and designer the ability to collaborate during an OTA procurement process. Period of Performance (POP): The projected construction timeline is approximately 1217 calendar days following the execution of the Phase 2 Construction modification. Product Service Code (PSC): Y1BG (Construction of Electronic and Communications Facilities). NAICS Code: 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction). INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES & FEEDBACK AREAS. In accordance with Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Design Instruction #3, the Government is seeking commercial industry feedback regarding the feasibility and market capacity for the following innovative methods: Modular and Off-Site Prefabrication: Fabricating large sections of the facility or complex mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems in factory-controlled environments to compress the construction schedule. 3D Printing: Utilizing large-scale 3D printing for secondary building components, non-load-bearing walls, or perimeter security fencing. Advanced Materials: Incorporating self-healing concrete to reduce lifecycle maintenance and maximize structural integrity, or utilizing high-performance insulation (e.g., aerogels or vacuum-insulated panels) to meet high-performance building standards. Submissions: Submit your capabilities statement and Market Intelligence response (attachment) via email toThomas Howard at Thomas.W.Howard@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Johnston at Nicholas.I.Johnston@usace.army.mil no later than Wednesday, September 23st, 2026 at 2:00 PM CDT (21:00 UTC). Use email subject: "Sources Sought Response: B21 Low Observable/Radio Frequency Hanger (LO/RF) Market Intel - [Your Firm Name]". File Naming Convention: Market Intel_B21 LO/RF_[FIRM NAME]

title: Wideband Remote Monitoring Sensor (WRMS) Enhancement and Sustainment (E&S)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small and large businesses to provide the required products and/or services. The WRMS E&S requirement falls under Project Officer Wideband Control as part of its mission to acquire and install state-of-the-art strategic satellite network control and planning systems for use with the Defense Satellite Communications System and Wideband Global Satellite Communications (WGS), and to provide satellite monitoring in either synchronized Spectrum Information Gathering or In-beam monitoring modes. At its most basic level, the primary function of WRMS is to aid the user with the identification and resolution of anomalies detected by the system. Anomalies are presented to the user through the comparison of planned versus actual radio frequency measurement data. The current contract, now in its last year of execution, provided a spectrum characterization and analysis software from the ground-up coding in micro-services that provided a Government-owned custom software that implements a hardware agnostic interface, all targeted to support the WGS-11 satellite while being able to support all prior WGS satellites. This software and hardware solution is integrated with all current Wideband Control interface subsystems and maintains current performance specifications. The desired end-result of this forthcoming contract is to sustain this fielded version of WRMS, WRMS version release 3 (WRMS v3.x), and to provide enhancements based on feedback from the users as well as to continue addressing current and new software backlog items. Please see the attached draft Performance Work Statement for more information.

description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requesting quotes for a service agreement and a qualification service for the CERULEAN SM450i Linear Cigarette Smoking Machine at TPL. This instrument is an integral component that support the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Office of the Chief Scientist/Office of Analytical and Regulatory Laboratories (OCS/OARL) to meet the legislative requirements and the sample workload that are an integral part of the Agency response to the legislation. This instrument is needed to develop methods for identifying and, in some cases, quantifying analytes in tobacco products under the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory jurisdiction and to establish expertise in the analyses of tobacco products. Service Agreement and Qualification Service CERULEAN SM450i Linear Cigarette Smoking Machine Background The Center for Tobacco Product (CTP) Tobacco Products Laboratory (TPL) located in Atlanta, Georgia has a requirement for a service and qualification agreement for one of its Cerulean SM450i Linear Cigarette Smoking Machines. This instrument is an integral component that supports the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Office of the Chief Scientist/Office of Analytical and Regulatory Laboratories (OCS/OARL) to meet the legislative requirements and the sample workload that are an integral part of the Agency response to the legislation. description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Laboratories and Scientific Services (LSS), intends to issue a purchase order to Orange Photonics, 176 Newport Road, New London, NH 03257, on a sole source basis for the purchase of two (2) portable cannabis analyzers for use in laboratory and field settings. title: Labeling Pilot for FDF Country of Origin, API Country of Origin, and KSM Country of Origin for Pharmaceutical Products
description: 1. Purpose The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Medical Supply Chain is conducting market research to identify U.S. or international pharmaceutical manufacturers that are willing to participate in a labeling pilot program. The pilot seeks to explore voluntary inclusion of additional product labeling data for Pharmaceutical Products identifying: Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, and responses do not commit the Government to any future acquisition or requirement. 2. Background DLA Troop Support Medical is evaluating methods to improve supply chain transparency, enhance traceability, and strengthen operational readiness by increasing visibility into the sourcing of pharmaceutical ingredients. Understanding FDF, API, and KSM origins helps support contingency planning, risk modeling, and alignment with emerging regulatory and strategic sourcing initiatives. The agency is exploring the feasibility of obtaining this information directly from manufacturers through voluntary labeling enhancements on packaging, shipping containers, or supplemental documentation. 3. Scope of Pilot The proposed labeling pilot will focus on a selected subset of generic pharmaceutical products purchased by DLA Troop Support Medical. Participating manufacturers may be asked to provide: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements DLA seeks to understand both operational feasibility and industry readiness. 4. Requested Information from Respondents Interested manufacturers are invited to submit a written response addressing the following: A. Company name, CAGE code, point of contact information B. Description of the pharmaceutical products you manufacture that are supplied or could be supplied to DLA C. Willingness to participate in a voluntary labeling or data?sharing pilot to include: Development of a labeling construct that contains all relevant sourcing information as outlined below. Obtaining approval of the labeling construct from the Food and Drug Administration. Producing labels with all required sourcing information and affixing them to products sold to the Department of War. D. Ability to provide the following information for each lot produced: API country of manufacture API country of origin (if different) Country of origin for the Finished Dose Form (FDF) Country of origin for each Key starting material (KSM) necessary for the production of each API If the country of origin of the API or KSM can vary by lot produced, DLA would be interested in the information specific to the labeled lot and to any previously produced lots Placement of this information on external packaging, product containers, or accompanying supply chain documentation Given the amount of information requested, inclusion of a QR code or link to additional information, or other methods of making the information accessible, could be considered Estimated production or administrative impact associated with adding these data elements E. Existing internal capabilities or systems that support API and KSM traceability and documentation F. Expected timeline and level of effort required to implement labeling modifications G. Any concerns, limitations, or cost impacts associated with participation H. Recommendations for structuring or scaling the pilot program 5. Submission Instructions Responses should be submitted via email in PDF or Word format to the DLA Troop Support Medical Supply Chain point of contact: Contracting Officer: Charles T. Reimer DLA Troop Support � Medical Supply Chain Email: Charles.Reimer@dla.mil Phone: 267-251-9370 (Cell)

title: Wideband Remote Monitoring Sensor (WRMS) Enhancement and Sustainment (E&S)
description: This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of small and large businesses to provide the required products and/or services. The WRMS E&S requirement falls under Project Officer Wideband Control as part of its mission to acquire and install state-of-the-art strategic satellite network control and planning systems for use with the Defense Satellite Communications System and Wideband Global Satellite Communications (WGS), and to provide satellite monitoring in either synchronized Spectrum Information Gathering or In-beam monitoring modes. At its most basic level, the primary function of WRMS is to aid the user with the identification and resolution of anomalies detected by the system. Anomalies are presented to the user through the comparison of planned versus actual radio frequency measurement data. The current contract, now in its last year of execution, provided a spectrum characterization and analysis software from the ground-up coding in micro-services that provided a Government-owned custom software that implements a hardware agnostic interface, all targeted to support the WGS-11 satellite while being able to support all prior WGS satellites. This software and hardware solution is integrated with all current Wideband Control interface subsystems and maintains current performance specifications. The desired end-result of this forthcoming contract is to sustain this fielded version of WRMS, WRMS version release 3 (WRMS v3.x), and to provide enhancements based on feedback from the users as well as to continue addressing current and new software backlog items. Please see the attached draft Performance Work Statement for more information.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for the Environmental Control System (ECS)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION INTRODUCTION THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. IT IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL BEING USED TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL AND ELIGIBLE BUSINESSES CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SUPPLIES/SERVICES DESCRIBED HEREIN, PRIOR TO DETERMINING THE METHOD OF ACQUISITION AND ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. ALL CAPABLE LARGE AND SMALL BUSINESSES THAT ARE INTERESTED ARE ENCOURAGED TO SEND IN A CAPABILITY PACKAGE. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) is seeking information from qualified companies that specialize in aviation Air Conditioning System (ACS) solutions for executive transport aircraft. Core capabilities required include systems engineering, requirements management, design, performance analysis, manufacturing, installation, testing and the ability to obtain a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airworthiness certification. NAVAIR will maintain life-cycle logistics responsibility. The company must be able to produce enough components to meet retrofit and supply demands within 18 months of contracting with the Government. Potential vendors, including commercial aviation suppliers, must be able to repair, refurbish, and modify existing components to satisfy readiness requirements. DISCLAIMER THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS RFI IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL VENDORS WITH CAPABILITY, TECHNICAL EXPERTISE AND CREDENTIALS TO MEET OUR HIGH STANDARDS FOR FUNCTIONALITY AND FINISH IN EXECUTIVE AVIATION INTERIORS. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT COMMITTED NOR OBLIGATED TO PAY FOR THE INFORMATION PROVIDED, AND NO BASIS FOR CLAIMS AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT SHALL ARISE AS A RESULT OF A RESPONSE TO THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS RFI DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE RFP, IF ISSUED. ELIGIBILITY The applicable NAICS code is 336413 � Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing. The Product Service Codes (PSC) is 1520- Aircraft, Rotary Wing, 1615 Helicopter Rotor Blades, Drive Mechanisms And Components, 1660 Aircraft Air Conditioning, Heating, And Pressurizing Equipment. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond and must clearly identify their business size (See Submission Information Paragraph 5). REQUIRED CAPABILITIES NAVAIR is seeking information for an executive aviation ACS solution that: Is capable of continuously running when outside Air Temperature (OAT) is between 50� F - 122� F. Has 50,000 BTU/hr. Cooling capacity. Integrates with existing ACS ducting, fresh air intake and gasper systems. Integrates with existing aircraft electrical power system and auxiliary power system. Integrates with airframe at the existing ACS component�s locations. Equipment and installation can be FAA certified by the OEM. Requirements: Must have Secret Facility Clearance. Must have FAA approved Designated Engineering Representative (DER), or Organization Designation Authorization (ODA) capabilities in support of obtaining supplemental type certificates Federal Aviation Regulation (FAR) Part 25 and 29 Supplemental Type Certificates (STCs). Must have FAR Part 21 Parts Manufacture Approval. Must be a FAR Part 145 certified Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility capable of handling interior components. SUBMISSION INFORMATION The requested information herein is to assist the Government in conducting market research to determine if potential business sources have the assets, skills, experience, financial stability, qualifications, rights to technical data, and knowledge required to support the requirements described herein. It is requested that interested businesses submit to the contracting office a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 10 pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum) demonstrating the ability to perform the tasks listed under the required capabilities. This documentation must address at a minimum the following: Company Name; Company Address; Company Business Size, and Point-of-Contact (POC) name, phone number, fax number, and e-mail address. Company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history, office location(s), CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Information on the current status of your company�s Facility Clearance and level. Prior/current corporate experience performing efforts similar in scope to the tasking described under Required Capabilities Section within the last five (5) years, if relevant- contract numbers, indication of whether as a prime or a subcontractor, contract values, point of contact with current telephone number, and a brief description of how the referenced contract relates to the proposed required capabilities and scope of performance. Respondents to this notice must also indicate whether they are a large business or qualify as a Small, Small Disadvantaged, Small Disadvantaged Veteran Owned, Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB), 8(a), Hub Zone or Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Concern. Responses shall be electronically submitted via email to Monica Card at monica.l.card.civ@us.navy.mil or Marie Hill at marie.n.hill5.civ.civ@us.navy.mil, in either Microsoft Word or Portable Document Format (PDF). The deadline for response to this request is 4:00 p.m., Eastern Standard Time, 23 September 2026. No phone calls will be accepted. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this request or to otherwise pay for the information collected. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. All information received in response to the RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY, will be handled accordingly. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted. The Government will not be liable for or suffer any consequential damages for any proprietary information not properly identified. Responses to this RFI will not be returned. Respondents will not be notified of the result of the review.

title: RFI-AMSS Integrator
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Arctic Mobility Sustainment System Integration IMPORTANT NOTICE The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) notice is to conduct market research to determine the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of potential business or government sources to perform system integration, kitting, packaging, and distribution for the Arctic Mobility Sustainment System (AMSS). This RFI does not constitute an Invitation for Bid (IFB), a Request for Proposal (RFP), a Request for Quote (RFQ) or an indication that the Government will contract for any of the items and/or services contained in this notice. This is not a request for proposals. No solicitation documents exist at this time. Any information provided does not constitute a proposal but will be considered an exchange of capabilities and ideas. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred in furnishing this information or potential participation in the event. This RFI does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that the Government will take procurement action in this matter. All information received in response to this notice that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses will be reviewed, and businesses of interest will be contacted. Additional information may be requested. The due date for responses is 23 SEP 2026. BACKGROUND & SCOPE The Arctic Mobility Sustainment System is the successor to the legacy Ahkio system. AMSS addresses the need for equipment to operate effectively in the Arctic environment, where the extreme cold, challenging terrain, and long distances require specialized capabilities. AMSS is being developed as a system that enables dismounted Soldiers to transport sustainment and survivability equipment essential for up to 72 hours. AMSS consists of an Arctic Transport (sled), Arctic Shelter, Arctic Heater, and related Component of End Items (COEI), and will have both a Team (5-man) and a Squad (10-man) configuration. Product Manager Force Sustainment Systems (PdM FSS) is evaluating industry and/or government capabilities to serve as a Lead System Integrator (LSI) to execute procurement, quality control, packaging, kitting, and final delivery of complete systems to designated CONUS and OCONUS end users. SEE ATTACHMENT For Component of End items (COEI) - Squad configuration & KITTING, PACKAGING, AND LOGISTICS STANDARDS Information requested from RESPONDENTS Please submit a white paper addressing the below listed information of interest. The white paper and any pertinent supplemental information must not exceed a combined length of 10 pages. Please structure your response according to the sections below. Do not attach marketing brochures, test reports, or other extraneous materials to your submission, as they will not be reviewed nor will they be considered as part of the evaluation. Electronic copies of responses should be in PDF format using size 12 font with one-inch margins. Following a review of the responses, PdM FSS may request additional information from respondents about their proposed capabilities. **For Arsenals and Depot respondents**: In addition to addressing each section below, please provide overarching acquisition strategy to include: Procurement Contracting Experience and Capability Describe overall integration capabilities, and any relevant experience conducting integration, kitting, and packaging efforts in support of the U.S. Government. For such cases, provide data on production capacity, time needed to ramp up production capacity, and throughput per month. Any available production metrics are welcomed. Provide CAGE code and SAM.gov active registration status. Integration Strategy Packaging Blueprints � Provide a packaging blueprint (one for Squad, one for Team) that adheres to the standards provided. Please include details of quality control and compliance with Government standards. Procurement � Describe strategy for procuring all COEI items, kit assembly and packaging, and shipment. Please address the following cost-saving opportunities in your response: Volume Discounting � Describe how your company will structure purchasing agreements with OEMs to capture maximum volume discounts. Long Lead Item Management � Identify which COEI components represent the highest cost and longest lead times. Propose strategies to mitigate price volatility and inflation. Kitting and Packaging Labor Efficiencies � Detail any packaging design options (such as custom-molded inserts, modular tool rolls, or nested component layouts) that would reduce the physical labor hours required to assemble, inspect, and verify each kit. Identify which items are best suited to remain in their original OEM packaging versus those requiring complete repackaging under MIL-STD-2073-1. Logistical & Freight Consolidation Strategies � Propose packaging arrangements inside or alongside the Arctic Transport (sled) that minimizes the overall cubic volume (cube) of the shipped kit, maximizing the number of units that can fit on a standard 463L military pallet or inside a standard ISO shipping container. Based on your established logistical footprint, propose optimal staging, warehousing, or transit nodes to minimize freight costs and transit risks when shipping to final destinations in NORTHCOM (Alaska (OCONUS) and lower 48 (CONUS) locations), PACOM (1st Special Forces Group in Japan), and EUCOM (10th Special Forces Group in Germany). Warehousing, Storage, and Facilities Strategies � Provide location(s) where the integration and packaging effort will be performed. Provide information on storage, available floor space, and on-site physical security. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Cost Estimate Assuming a destination of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, identify logistics, staging, packaging and freight costs for the shipment of: 2,000 AMSS Squad Kits Assume a COEI procurement cost of $25,000 per unit. 1,000 AMSS Team Kits Assume a COEI procurement cost of $20,000 per unit. Risk Identification and Mitigation Identify potential risks in the following areas and propose a mitigation strategy for each: Supply Chain Risk � NDAA Section 889 compliance, long product lead times, and price volatility. Integration Risk � Ensuring kit accuracy and quality assurance. Logistics Risk � Physical security of system items at integration facility, shipping to remote locations, and transportation damage (including sharp items damaging other items inside packaging). Point of Contact Provide name, email, and phone number for company representative(s). The Government team will contact respondents if there is continued interest. The Government team reserves the right to request additional information from all respondents. title: UT NP ARCH 100(2) Bridges on Delicate Arch Road
description: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. This existing condition produces flooding and sediment deposition, which creates unsafe conditions for visitors, triggers road closures, potentially strands Park visitors, diminishes visitor experience of the Park, and generates high operational costs associated with traffic management, visitor safety, and cleanup operations. SCOPE OF THE WORK: This project will be designated as Reconstruction (4R) with one segment of restoration (3R), and will design and construct 100� span concrete bridges at the Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash. The DA roadway profile at each Wash will be raised to accommodate a 10-year design frequency and allow a medium-sized excavator to access each wash. The DA will be realigned at the Salt Valley wash, moving the roadway and new bridge location to the north of the existing roadway and drainage crossing. The remaining 3R sections of the roadway will receive full depth reclamation (FDR) or removal of pavement, including all parking areas, followed by a 4-inch pavement overlay. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20420-0000 Embankment Construction: 10,000 CUYD 25101-0300 Placed Riprap, Class 3: 1,725 CUYD 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 5,140 TON 40101-5600 Asphalt Concrete Pavement, Gyratory Mix, 1/2-Inch or 3/4-Inch Nominal Maximum Size Aggregate, 0.3 To <3 Million ESAL: 8,300 TON 55201-0200 Structural Concrete, Class A (AE): 752 CUYD 55401-2000 Reinforcing Steel, Epoxy Coated: 138,000 LB 55601-1100 Bridge Railing, Steel, Two Rail: 642 LNFT 56501-0200 Drilled Shaft, 24-Inch Diameter: 750 LNFT 56501-0300 Drilled Shaft, 30-Inch Diameter: 890 LNFT 60901-1300 Curb, Concrete, 15-Inch Depth (Reinforced, Colored): 3,921 LNFT 61701-4500 Guardrail System Mgs, Type 2, Class A Steel Posts: 1,290 LNFT 63506-0500 Temporary Traffic Control, Flagger: 5,800 HOUR ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � November 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � December 2028 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000 This will be solicited as a full and open competition.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for Mobile Cyber Analytic Toolkits
description: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source, NextCom LLC (dba NextComputing), for the reprocurement of thirty (30) Mobile Cyber Analytic Toolkits and associated embedded software, documentation, training, warranty, and related deliverables. The Government requires delivery of the first three (3) kits within 30 days after award to support testing, validation, and authorization activities prior to fielding the remaining units. In addition to meeting the required delivery schedule, the contractor must provide a conforming solution that satisfies the technical specifications and interfaces with the current Government Big Data Platform. This acquisition is being conducted under 41 U.S.C. 1901, as implemented through the revised FAR Part 12 procedures adopted by DoD Class Deviation DARS Tracking Number 2026-O0028.This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations. No solicitation document is available. However, any responsible source that believes it can satisfy the requirement may submit a capability statement that demonstrates its ability to: (1) deliver the first three (3) kits within 30 days after award; (2) satisfy the required technical specifications; and (3) provide a conforming solution that interfaces with the current Government Big Data Platform. Submissions must be received by the point of contact identified in this notice no later than 23 September 2026 at 16:00 EDT. Capability statements will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

The Government has made every effort to accurately reflect the requirements and information contained in this solicitation. However, if there are any inconsistencies between the executive summary and the solicitation, the solicitation will govern. 1. The U.S. Air Force 87 Contracting Squadron (CONS), Joint Base MDL, New Jersey, on behalf of the USAF Expeditionary Center (EC) located on JB-MDL, NJ. has a requirement for providing Fieldcraft Training Support Services in accordance with Performance Work Statement (PWS) (Section 1.2, Attachment 0001) dated 19 MAY 2026. Services shall be provided for one (1) 12-month period plus four (4) 12-month option periods from 12 DEC 2026 � 11 DEC 2031. In addition, the government may extend the total length of the contract by no more than (6) months after the end of the last option year, if necessary, and IAW with RFO 52.217-8. 2. The Government intends to award a single Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Requirements Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). The acquisition is based upon competition to represent the Best Value IAW RFO 15.101 to the Government. For proposal instructions and submittal information, see RFO 52.212-1, entitled Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services. For the basis of award, see RFO 52.212-2, entitled Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services. 3. The contracting officer has determined there is a high probability of adequate price competition in this acquisition. Upon examination of the initial offers, the contracting officer will review this determination and if, in the contracting officer's opinion, adequate price competition exists no additional data will be requested and certification under RFO 15.403-4 will not be required. However, if at any time during this competition the contracting officer determines that adequate price competition no longer exists; offerors may be required to submit cost data to the extent necessary for the contracting officer to determine the reasonableness and affordability of the price. 4. This is an all-electronic solicitation release. Hard copies are not available. The Government will post all information pertaining to the solicitation and award of this requirement to the Government Point of Entry (GPE), also known as SAM.gov. It is the responsibility of each offeror to review the web page for postings of amendments, updates, or changes to current information. 5. Offerors are required to meet all solicitation requirements, such as terms and conditions, representations and certifications, and technical requirements, in addition to those identified as evaluation factors. Failure to meet a requirement may result in an offer being ineligible for award. Offerors must clearly identify any exception to the solicitation terms and conditions and provide complete accompanying rationale. 6. Questions regarding this RFP shall be submitted via email, and subsequent answers will be posted to SAM.gov. If Offerors have questions, they are requested to submit them in writing grouped by solicitation section and make reference to the particular section / subsection number. Questions must be received via email no later than 5 August 2026 at 1600 Eastern Time to both Christina Vargas at christina.vargas.1@us.af.mil and lewis.hampton@us.af.mil. The decision whether to respond to questions and requests for clarification made after Q&A suspense date closing shall be at the sole discretion of the Contracting Officer. Failure of a prospective offeror to submit any questions will be construed to mean that the prospective offeror fully understands all requirements of the solicitation. 7. Clarifications: Clarifications, exchanges of information between Government and offerors, will be controlled by the Contracting Officer. The Government intends to award a contract without negotiations with respective offerors. The Government, however, reserves the right to conduct negotiations if deemed in its best interest. 8. Proposals submitted in response to this RFP must be submitted via email to both Christina Vargas at christina.vargas.1@us.af.mil and lewis.hampton@us.af.mil. Proposals not sent to both addresses will be considered nonresponsive and will not be evaluated forward. To ensure successful delivery, contractors shall obtain confirmation from the Contracting Officer that their proposal has been received and reviewed. Email submissions can occasionally be misplaced or routed to junk folders, so it is the contractor's responsibility to secure direct confirmation from the Contracting Officer that the government has both received and acknowledged their proposal. Failure to obtain email confirmation of receipt from the Government may result in your offer not being received and, consequently, not being evaluated. title: USDA-ARS Tifton Roofing Remodel
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12C0BA26Q0011 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for USDA-ARS Tifton Roofing Remodel. The objective for this project is to replace aging roofing materials with identical 26 gauge (field verify) standing seam metal roofs on multiple location buildings to enhance the productivity of each building in support of USDA-ARS research mission objectives. The magnitude of this construction project is between $250,000 and $500,000. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 238160-Roofing Contractors. The small business size standard is $19M. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Bid, Performance, and Payment Bonds are required. An organized site visit has been scheduled for Thursday, September 17, 2026, at 2:00 pm Eastern Time (ET). Contractors wishing to attend the site visit must register by emailing Joel Blanchett at Joel.Blanchett@usda.gov by September 16, 2026, by 4:00 PM Eastern Time with the name(s) of attendee(s), company they are with, and company(s) they are representing. A Government issued photo ID is required for attendance. The site visit will be held for the purpose of providing contractors with the opportunity to familiarize themselves with the site, which may be helpful in the preparation of quotes. Attendance at the site visit is not mandatory for quote submission; however, failure to visit the site will not relieve or mitigate the successful contractor�s responsibility and obligation to fully comply with the terms, conditions, and specifications contained and/or referenced in this document.

title: Intent to Sole Source to an SDVOSB � Bed Bug Pest Control Services � Cleveland VA Medical Center
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE TO A SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (SDVOSB) The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 10 (NCO 10), intends to award a sole-source contract to CDS Services Inc., a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), for bed bug pest control services in support of the Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center and associated VA facilities. REQUIREMENT The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, transportation, supplies, materials, and equipment necessary to perform bed bug pest management services. Services include bed bug inspections, treatments, follow-up inspections, and related Integrated Pest Management (IPM) services on an as-needed basis. Services may be required during regular business hours, after hours, and on weekends at the Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center and associated VA facilities identified in the Performance Work Statement. NAICS: 561710 - Exterminating and Pest Control Services PSC: S207 - Housekeeping - Insect/Rodent Control ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE October 3, 2026 through October 2, 2027 PRIMARY PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center 10701 East Boulevard Cleveland, OH 44106 Services may also be required at associated VA facilities identified in the Performance Work Statement. SOLE-SOURCE AUTHORITY The anticipated value of this acquisition is below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT). The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to award this requirement using other than competitive procedures pursuant to 38 U.S.C. 8127(b), as implemented by VAAR 813.106-70(b) and the VA Veterans First Contracting Program. The Contracting Officer intends to exercise the statutory authority provided under 38 U.S.C. 8127(b) to make a sole-source award to CDS Services Inc. Competition is not being sought for this acquisition because the Contracting Officer is exercising the VA's statutory authority to award a procurement below the SAT to an eligible SDVOSB using procedures other than competitive procedures. In accordance with VAAR 819.7008, a determination that only one SDVOSB can meet the requirement is not required when exercising this sole-source authority. The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated award can be made at a fair and reasonable price and that use of the sole-source authority is in the best interest of the Government. NOTICE This Special Notice is provided for informational purposes only. It is not a Request for Quotations (RFQ), Request for Proposals (RFP), or solicitation for competitive offers. The Government is not requesting quotations, proposals, or capability statements in response to this notice. The Department of Veterans Affairs does not intend to issue a competitive solicitation as a result of this notice. The Department of Veterans Affairs intends to proceed with a sole-source award to CDS Services Inc.

title: Blood Bank Plasma Storage Freezers and Blood Bank Refrigerator
description: Blood Bank Plasma Storage Freezers and Blood Bank Refrigerator Notice Type: Presolicitation Notice / Notice of Intent Agency: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC) Department: Department of Transfusion Medicine/Transfusion Services Laboratory (DTM/TSL) NAICS Code: 339113 � Surgical Appliance and Supplies Manufacturing PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Response Date: September 23, 2026, at 4:30 PM ET The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Clinical Center (CC), Department of Transfusion Medicine/Transfusion Services Laboratory (DTM/TSL), has a requirement for two (2) Blood Bank Plasma Storage (-30�C) Freezers and one (1) Blood Bank Refrigerator, including delivery, setup, and service plans. The equipment is required to support the safe storage of blood products used for Clinical Center patients. The Government intends to procure the following Helmer equipment: One (1) Helmer iBF120-GX, 20 cu. ft. Blood Bank Plasma Storage Freezer with metal drawers; One (1) Helmer iBF120-GX, 20 cu. ft. Blood Bank Plasma Storage Freezer with shelves; and One (1) Helmer iBR113-GX, 13 cu. ft. Blood Bank Refrigerator. The existing refrigerator is experiencing temperature excursions that could affect blood-product purity and potency, while the existing freezers have undergone multiple repairs and are nearing the end of their useful lives. Failure of this equipment could result in the loss of critical or irreplaceable blood products and negatively affect patient care. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order to Helmer, Inc. The Helmer units meet DTM's regulatory and licensing requirements and will standardize equipment within the Transfusion Services Laboratory. The units provide continuous electronic temperature monitoring, temperature-excursion alarms, door-open alarms, appropriate footprints for the laboratory environment, and frost-free operation. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources that believe they can provide equipment meeting the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement and supporting documentation for consideration. Responses must demonstrate the vendor's ability to provide equipment that meets all technical, regulatory, licensing, delivery, setup, and service requirements. Responses are due no later than September 23, 2026, at 4:30 PM Eastern Time and must be emailed to shasheshe.goolsby@nih.gov and reference POTS 26-010215. The Government will consider all timely responses received before proceeding with the intended award.

title: SEI Industries, Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), "Premo Fireballs" Aerial Ignition Sphere Dispenser Purchase and Reburbishment
description: SPECIAL NOTICE: 1202SC26Q2718 Description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE The U.S. Forest Service (USFS), Procurement & Property Services (PPS), Incident Procurement Operations (IPO), At Incident Management Support Branch (AIMS), intends to issue a Firm Fixed Priced Purchase Order as authorized by 41 U.S.C. 1901 - FAR 12.201-1, Simplified Procedures, on or about October 1, 2026, to Fire Ignition Resources, LLC, for the USDA Forest Service (USDA-FS). The intent of this requirement is to provide one (1) refurbishment and an estimated five (5) new Premo Fireballs Aerial Ignition Plastic Sphere Dispensers to be used during prescribed burning and wildfire incidents. The Premo MK IIIs are the only aerial ignition devices in USDA-FS inventory and the only aerial ignition device authorized for use by the Wildland Fire Aerial Ignition Operations as directed by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) PMS 501, Chapter 3. By awarding a Purchase Order for the supply of SEI Industries, Premo MK III Plastic Sphere Dispensers through Fire Ignition Resources, LLC, the USDA/Forest Service ensures equipment performance, OEM equipment support, operational reliability, system continuity, operator and equipment safety, and existing factory warranties, while ensuring maximum mission readiness, meeting the strategic objectives of the Wildland Fire Aerial Ignition Operations of our organization. The PPS, IPO, AIMS intends to non-competitively award this requirement to Fire Ignition Resources, LLC. The required items are proprietary to SEI Industries, LLC and the only authorized vendor to provide SEI Industries, Premo MK III dispensers, is Fire Ignition Resources, LLC. Furthermore, Premo MK IIIs are compatible in all aspects with existing SEI Industries systems/equipment presently in use, allowing personnel in the field to maintain continuity of service during fire mission times. No other manufacturer is compatible or can interchange with SEI Industries� proprietary systems without voiding existing warranties and posing safety risks to equipment and operators. As a result, any vendor other than Fire Ignition Resources, LLC capable of providing comparable models would not be approved by the manufacturer or per established USDA-FS equipment approvals. Fire Ignition Resources, LLC is the only source capable of providing the authorized required items to maintain the safety of personnel, equipment, continuity of service, and the uninterrupted operation and mission readiness during fire seasons. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 332994 with the size standard of 1000 employees. This notice of intent is not a request for proposals or quotes. However, all responsible sources may submit an offer and capabilities/narrative that proves by clear and convincing evidence that detail their ability to provide proprietary Premo MK III dispensers authorized by SEI Industries, LLC. If said OFFER and capabilities/narrative is received within fifteen (15) calendar days of publication of this notice, the narrative will be considered by the Contracting Officer. All responses shall be submitted to the Government point of contact at the email address shown below. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Government Point of Contact: Purchasing Agent Shannon Meadows, shannon.meadows@usda.gov.
